title: Canonical bisimulation-congruence saturation
boundary: The construction changes only resonance, preserves the source boundary/type/glue behavioral quotient, and gives the least three-coordinate congruent extension; it is not a quotient Incidence construction on the quotient carrier.

title: Resonance-saturation reflection
boundary: This first reflection is fiberwise over the pointwise ordered resonance extensions of one fixed incidence skeleton; the carrier-changing categorical extension is stated separately in spine 33.

title: Global resonance-saturation adjunction
boundary: Carrier and cell type may vary, but the role type is fixed; morphisms must preserve unit, selected glue, boundary occurrences, resonance, and bisimulation. No role-changing or boundary-reflecting maps are claimed.

title: Role-changing exact-boundary saturation adjunction
boundary: Morphisms may change carrier, role, and cell type and reflect membership only for mapped boundary occurrences; essential surjectivity onto all target boundary occurrences is not required.

title: Globally boundary-surjective saturation adjunction
boundary: Every target boundary occurrence must have a source object/occurrence preimage, but target cells with empty boundary need not lie in the carrier map image; carrier surjectivity is not claimed.

title: Carrier-and-boundary-surjective saturation adjunction
boundary: Morphisms must cover every target carrier point and boundary occurrence but need not be injective; this is the strongest morphism class currently formalized, not a claim that weaker classes are invalid.

title: Saturation internal-logic conservativity
boundary: The unconditional result is one-way preservation for the implication-free positive fragment; full preservation/reflection, including implication, is equivalent to source quotient congruence. IncProof results require the stated semantic-agreement hypotheses.

title: Dependent-calculus saturation conservativity
boundary: The theorem transfers an existing normalized completion, which already assumes associativity and quotient congruence; saturation does not manufacture those laws for an arbitrary resonance. The IncDepCompletionModel interpreter is incidence-independent and is retained exactly.

title: Associative saturation completion
boundary: Associativity preservation requires source mode transport along bisimilar inputs; it is not claimed for arbitrary associative resonance. The strict Bool example has total bisimulation and gains output modes under saturation.

title: Exact quotient-associativity criterion
boundary: The exact criterion is associativity of the existential quotient relation; mode transport is only a sufficient source-level hypothesis. Quotient associativity may be stated directly even when source resonance does not descend exactly.

title: Saturation-associativity obstruction classification
boundary: The finite table is defined noncomputably using classical decidability; it is a complete finite certificate theorem, not yet a native executable enumerator or minimized orbit classification.

title: Executable associativity-obstruction decision
boundary: Execution requires user-supplied exact Boolean checkers for source bisimulation and resonance. The table is not yet quotiented by automorphisms or support-minimized.

title: Ternary interaction representation
boundary: The theorem represents arbitrary small ternary relational systems, not arbitrary categories or dependent type theories. Boundaries and cell types are trivial in this first representation; fullness into all structured Incidence maps is not claimed.

title: Small-category composition representation
boundary: The construction represents the arrow-composition theory of arbitrary small categories and maps functors to resonance homomorphisms. Object and hom recovery is supplied by spine 45, and scoped fullness by spine 47; higher categories are not included here.

title: Internal category recovery
boundary: Objects are recovered as the image of the known identity-arrow embedding and homs as known endpoint fibers. Intrinsic identity recovery is supplied by spine 46 and scoped fullness by spine 47; univalence and higher coherence are not included here.

title: Intrinsic identity and object recovery
boundary: The identity predicate uses endpoint projections in addition to the ternary relation. It does not eliminate endpoints, prove univalence, or higher-category coherence; scoped fullness is supplied by spine 47.

title: Scoped fullness and exact functor image
boundary: Fullness is proved precisely for homomorphisms carrying object and hom actions satisfying identity, composition, and exact-arrow agreement. Arbitrary ternary-relation homomorphisms need not preserve endpoints or identities, so unrestricted fullness is not claimed.

title: Pure relational category recovery
boundary: The recovery predicates mention only the ternary composition relation and equality on its arrow carrier. The construction and correctness proofs still use the originating category; the abstract recognition direction is supplied separately by spine 49. This is not a univalence result.

title: Relational category recognition
boundary: The axioms are sufficient to construct a category and necessary for every represented small category composition system. Both directions of composability are required: matching endpoints produce a mode and every mode has matching endpoints. The explicit system round trip is supplied by spine 50; axiom independence/minimality, univalence, and higher coherence are not proved.

title: Relational category system round trip
boundary: The isomorphism is between ternary resonance systems and uses classical choice to select the unique endpoint identities and composites. It does not claim an equivalence of categories of all models and morphisms, axiom minimality, univalence, or higher coherence.

title: Functorial relational category reconstruction
boundary: Morphisms are required to preserve both resonance and pure identities; bare relation homomorphisms do not suffice. Reconstruction is functorial on every hom and the round-trip maps are natural. The single Cat-valued functor is supplied by spine 52; a bundled categorical equivalence is not claimed.

title: Cat-valued reconstruction functor
boundary: The functor is universe-explicit from recognized ternary systems to mathlib `Cat` and packages the previously checked homwise construction. The inverse-direction functor is supplied by spine 53; natural isomorphisms of the composites and a categorical equivalence are not included here.

title: Category recognition inverse-direction functor
boundary: This is the inverse-direction functor from mathlib `Cat` to recognized ternary systems. The recognized-side natural isomorphism is supplied by spine 54; the Cat-side natural isomorphism and categorical equivalence are not included here.

title: Recognized-system round-trip natural isomorphism
boundary: This proves the recognized-system-side natural isomorphism `𝟭 ≅ reconstruction ⋙ recognition`. The Cat-side natural isomorphism and the final categorical equivalence are not included.

title: Category round-trip equivalence
boundary: For every Cat object, the original category is equivalent to its reconstructed category via a full, faithful, essentially surjective canonical functor. Functor naturality is supplied by spine 56; a strict Cat-valued natural isomorphism and global 1-categorical equivalence are not included here.

title: Category round-trip functor naturality
boundary: The canonical full/faithful/essential-surjective functors commute exactly with every original functor on objects and homs. This is a naturality square of category equivalences, not yet a natural isomorphism in the 1-category Cat; the distinction between categorical equivalence and strict Cat isomorphism remains explicit.

title: Relational-category comparison capstone
boundary: The package contains both directional functors, a recognized-side natural isomorphism, Cat-side objectwise equivalences, and exact naturality squares. It is deliberately not declared as a 1-categorical equivalence between model categories because Cat isomorphism is stricter than equivalence of categories; a native bicategorical pseudonatural-equivalence package remains future work.

title: Dependent judgment interaction representation
boundary: For each fixed raw context, formation and typing judgments are represented exactly and derivation-preserving renamings act functorially. This is a faithful representation of the existing raw Pi/Sigma/Identity calculus, not a sound-and-complete internal language for arbitrary ResonanceSpec models.

title: General resonance-law internal language
boundary: The axiom schema and soundness theorem work over arbitrary carriers without finite enumeration. They characterize the first-order-free propositional content of ResonanceSpec exactly, but strong Kripke completeness for the potentially infinite schema is not claimed.

title: General resonance-law Kripke semantics
boundary: Kripke soundness holds for the full potentially infinite schema without carrier enumeration. Strong completeness is not claimed: it is proved equivalent to the explicit remaining gate of constructing one lawful Kripke countermodel for every nonderivable formula.

title: Countable infinite-schema strong completeness
boundary: Strong Kripke completeness holds for arbitrary finite or infinite resonance carriers whose resonance-atom language has CountableAtomCoding. The proof does not establish an enumeration-free completeness theorem for uncountable atom languages.

title: Enumeration-free resonance-law completeness
boundary: Zorn-based prime extension removes CountableAtomCoding and proves strong completeness for arbitrary same-universe atom types and resonance carriers. The construction is classical and depends on choice; it does not claim predicative or choice-free completeness.

title: Dependent judgment proof-theoretic semantics
boundary: Soundness holds for every predicate model closed under the raw inference rules, and the syntactic model is exact, least, and stable under renaming and substitution. This is proof-theoretic term-model completeness, not extensional set-valued, CwF, categorical, normalization, or equality completeness.

title: Dependent contextual-category comprehension
boundary: Well-formed contexts and proof-erased well-typed substitutions form a strict category; raw types reindex functorially, and context extension has display projection, generic variable, and unique substitution pairing. A fully bundled CwF with well-formed type and term presheaves remains separate.

title: Dependent type-and-term presheaves and terminal residual
boundary: Well-formed types and total typed terms reindex strictly and contravariantly, with natural type projection. Because substitutions retain unconstrained Nat components, the empty context has distinct identity and constant-unit endomorphisms and is not terminal; a full CwF requires finite-context extensionalization or normalized substitutions.

title: Dependent scoped syntax and finite-support substitution
boundary: Formation and typing derivations bound every de Bruijn variable by context length. Consequently substitutions agreeing on the finite context act identically on all well-formed types and well-typed terms. This supplies the congruence needed for the corrected quotient category.

title: Finite-support context quotient and terminal object
boundary: Substitutions are quotiented by agreement on actual target variables; composition descends using scopedness, and the quotient forms a strict category whose empty context is terminal. Type and term presheaves have not yet been descended from the representative category to this quotient category.

title: Finite-support type and typed-term presheaves
boundary: Well-formed types and total typed terms descend to the corrected quotient category independently of representatives. Both satisfy strict identity and composition laws, and the typed-term projection is natural. Terms are currently represented by their total space rather than a separately bundled fiber over each type.

title: Finite-support comprehension universality
boundary: Context extension, display projection, generic term, substitution pairing, both defining equations, and uniqueness descend to the corrected quotient category. Together with spines 67–68 this supplies all semantic data of a syntactic CwF; the explicit dependent term-fiber package is supplied by spine 70.

title: Bundled finite syntactic category with families
boundary: Terms are explicit fibers over the type presheaf, reindex dependently, and connect to the generic term and universal pairing. One certificate combines terminal context, Ty/Tm substitution, and split comprehension. This is a syntactic CwF; a CwF morphism into the existing set-valued semantics is separate.

title: Completed-fragment CwF semantic comparison
boundary: Fully coherent completed judgments embed conservatively into the finite syntactic CwF and carry set-valued interpretations coherent with identity substitution. This is a judgment-level comparison on the completed fragment, not a CwF morphism on all raw judgments; general substitution and comprehension naturality remain separate.

title: Completed-fragment substitution naturality
boundary: For every completed judgment and semantically realized raw substitution, finite-CwF reindexing is raw substitution exactly and the set-valued interpretation commutes with that substitution. Existence of semantic realizations for all raw substitutions and comprehension naturality remain explicit gates; a whole-CwF morphism is not claimed.

title: Completed-fragment comprehension naturality
boundary: Corresponding syntactic and set-valued extensions and pairings are constructed from the same completed judgment and semantic substitution. Projection and generic equations hold on both sides, and the semantic generic component equals the transported interpretation of the syntactically substituted term. Global judgment completion and semantic-substitution coverage remain required for a whole-CwF morphism.

title: Whole-CwF morphism readiness boundary
boundary: Every completed judgment now has a canonical semantic realization of identity substitution. All local judgment, substitution, and comprehension laws are packaged with an exact iff: total promotion requires precisely completion of every finite-CwF term and semantic realization of every raw substitution. These two global coverage statements are not proved here, so a total CwF morphism is not claimed.

title: Completed display-projection semantics
boundary: Every completed display type now canonically realizes the nonidentity raw projection substitution. Its semantic map is the set-valued Sigma projection, its replacements are weakened semantic lookups, and its finite-support class is exactly the syntactic CwF display projection. Arbitrary substitution coverage and global judgment completion remain open.

title: Semantic-substitution composition and finite functoriality
boundary: Raw substitutions and their semantic maps and replacements compose, and completed realizations are closed under precomposition by target-independent realizations. The induced finite-support morphism is exactly categorical composition. This closure theorem does not construct a realization for every raw substitution, so arbitrary substitution coverage and global judgment completion remain open.

title: Completed-term semantic pairing realization
boundary: A realized base substitution and completed target term canonically produce a target-independent semantic realization of their raw comprehension pairing. Its semantic map is set-valued Sigma pairing and its finite-support class is exactly the syntactic CwF pairing. An arbitrary substitution head need not be the reindexing of a completed target term, so this theorem does not by itself prove global substitution coverage.

title: General source-side semantic pairing realization
boundary: An arbitrary well-typed source-side head extends any realized base substitution once semantic formation transport and a source semantic term are supplied. The resulting target-independent realization satisfies semantic projection and generic equations and recovers exactly the quotient-CwF pairing. Global coverage is reduced to supplying these explicit formation and typing semantic data uniformly; that supply theorem is not claimed here.

title: Canonical raw-substitution pairing decomposition
boundary: Every substitution into an extended target canonically decomposes into its tail and newest well-typed component. Components agree exactly, proof-erased substitutions are equal, and the finite quotient class is exactly the CwF pairing. Raw substitutions retain proof-relevant derivations, so unrestricted Leibniz equality before proof erasure is intentionally not asserted. Semantic coverage is thereby reduced recursively to semantic data for the head components.

title: Recursive semantic-substitution realization induction
boundary: Semantic realization is invariant under changes of proof-relevant substitution witnesses with the same term function. Empty targets are realized canonically, and a realized canonical tail plus general semantic data for the actual head realizes the original substitution. Thus global coverage has an exact recursive induction principle; uniform synthesis of the per-head formation and typing semantic data remains open.

title: Intrinsic lookup-coherent semantic substitutions
boundary: A strengthened realization now internalizes, for every target lookup, a fiber equivalence from the replacement family to the reindexed target family and equality of the transported replacement term with the reindexed target variable. Identity and completed display projections inhabit this interface with their exact target semantic trees. Pairing and composition closure for the strengthened interface and global per-head synthesis remain open.

title: Lookup-coherent pairing and composition closure
boundary: Target-independent realizations compose generically, and intrinsic lookup coherence is preserved by composition through reindexed fiber equivalences and by arbitrary source-side pairing through the head formation equivalence and inherited tail coherence. The semantic maps remain exact. Uniform synthesis of per-head semantic formation and typing data is now the remaining substitution-coverage gate.

title: Strengthened coherent whole-CwF readiness boundary
boundary: The public totality boundary is strengthened to canonical-model-anchored, lookup-coherent substitution coverage. This stronger gate implies the previous coverage and readiness packages and is exactly conjoined with judgment completion. Neither global gate is proved here; uniform judgment completion and coherent per-head semantic synthesis remain open.

title: Recursive lookup-coherent substitution induction
boundary: The recursive substitution-coverage induction is lifted completely to the intrinsic lookup-coherent interface. Proof-witness transport preserves map and target tree, empty targets are automatic, and a coherent tail plus semantic data for the actual head realizes the original substitution coherently. Uniform per-head formation and typing semantic synthesis remains the only premise before this induction yields global coherent coverage.

title: Readiness-aligned context semantic synthesis
boundary: Coherent formation-readiness and the semantic telescope it generates are indexed in one dependent structure. Canonical synthesis constructs that aligned tree, and erasure recovers the existing dependent result/tree package exactly. This removes proof-object drift between readiness and semantics; uniform semantic synthesis for arbitrary source-side head terms remains open.

title: Exact source-head semantic coverage boundary
boundary: Canonical formation preservation already generates the source/target formation fiber for every coherent tail realization. The only new local assumption is semantic interpretation of the arbitrary well-typed source head; it builds an exact general pairing head and closes the coherent recursive extension step for the original proof-relevant substitution. Global discharge of this typing-only coverage assumption remains open.

title: Two-sided coherent semantic substitutions
boundary: The strengthened substitution interface retains semantic trees at both source and target, supplying the missing source telescope required for arbitrary source-term interpretation. Identity, empty targets, proof-witness replacement, and source-head extension preserve the exact source tree. Discharging typing-only coverage still requires coherent readiness and alignment of the interpreted source-head type with the formation dispatcher result.

title: Source-head readiness and type-alignment discharge
boundary: A coherently ready source-head judgment is interpreted by canonical typing dispatch along the identity on the retained source tree. A fiber equivalence aligns that identity interpretation with the source formation generated along the semantic tail. Transport then constructs the formerly assumed typing semantic result, so global aligned-readiness coverage implies the complete typing-only source-head coverage gate. Constructing readiness and alignment for every raw substitution component remains open.

title: Global two-sided substitution realization
boundary: The local arbitrary-head constructor is iterated over every coherent target telescope. Typing-only coverage, and hence the stronger readiness/alignment coverage, realizes every raw substitution two-sided coherently while retaining the supplied source semantic result/tree exactly. The target semantic result is existential rather than forced to the canonical completion-model synthesis; canonical target anchoring remains the next equality gate.

title: Formation target-invariance boundary
boundary: The exact target-anchoring law states that canonical formation preservation depends on the target semantic tree but not the source context, substitution, semantic source, or replacement witnesses. Base and unit satisfy this law definitionally. Under the general law, every arbitrary source-head formation has exactly the canonical identity-dispatch target interpretation. Mutual formation/typing induction remains required for Pi, Sigma, and Identity.

title: Mutual target-invariance induction motives
boundary: Dependent target type and term outputs are exposed for comparison, while the typing motive records target-formation equality and heterogeneous target-term equality without constraining irrelevant source fields. Formation and typing target-invariance are mutually recursive local motives. Formation base/unit and typing unit are unconditional. Variable closure requires an explicit source-independence law because the current variable provider is intentionally unconstrained; this law is now isolated exactly rather than silently assumed.

title: Pi/Sigma constructor target equations
boundary: Strict Pi and Sigma formation dispatch expose target formation results definitionally assembled from their recursive domain and codomain target results. These projection equations reduce outer-constructor target equality to recursive equality plus transport of the extended target tree and lifted replacements. They are structural equations, not yet the full Pi/Sigma invariance closure.

title: Dependent formation target packages
boundary: A Sigma package binds a domain formation result to a codomain result over precisely its extended semantic context. Pi and Sigma target formation become ordinary functions of this package, so package equality implies outer target equality by congruence. Strict constructor outputs equal these package functions definitionally. The remaining transport problem is reduced to equality of the recursive dependent packages.

title: Recursive Pi/Sigma target invariance
boundary: Domain invariance identifies the dependent target index. A canonical package function transports that equality, while codomain invariance compares each lifted run with identity dispatch on its exact extended target tree. Package congruence closes Pi and Sigma formation target invariance. Identity formation and the remaining typing cases remain outside this theorem.

title: Identity target package and normalization boundary
boundary: A dependent package binds the carrier semantic type and both Identity endpoints in its exact fiber; package equality implies outer Identity formation equality, and strict dispatch satisfies the package equation definitionally. Recursive typing invariance alone does not control transports chosen by the unconstrained rebase provider, so normalized endpoint source-independence is isolated as an explicit law. Under that exact law, the Identity formation motive closes.

title: Canonical-provenance-scoped rebase
boundary: The unrestricted rebase provider assumed by the old preservation interface is proved impossible already at universe zero. Restricting rebase requests to results with provenance from one shared canonical formation makes the provider automatically constructible by uniqueness. Typing normalization can therefore be performed without the impossible global hypothesis. A provider-free canonical mutual dispatcher already exists elsewhere in the development; the remaining migration is to restate target invariance over that dispatcher rather than the obsolete interface.

title: Dispatcher-parametric target invariance
boundary: Formation and typing target invariance are restated directly over an explicit strict mutual dispatcher, eliminating the impossible unrestricted rebase provider from the logical objective. The old statement is exactly recovered by specialization, while the existing scoped canonical strict preservation dispatcher now receives the authoritative formation and typing invariance objectives. Constructor closure over this scoped dispatcher remains to be proved.

title: Scoped canonical base/unit/Pi/Sigma target invariance
boundary: On the provider-free scoped canonical dispatcher, base and unit target invariance hold definitionally. Pi and Sigma dispatch definitionally expose recursive dependent target packages; a dispatcher-parametric package argument transports domain equality and anchors both codomain executions to identity, closing both constructors. Identity formation and typing constructors remain.

title: Scoped typing target-invariance base and variable boundary
boundary: The dispatcher-parametric typing objective is localized and proved equivalent to its global form. On the scoped canonical dispatcher, unit typing closes definitionally, while variable typing closes under its exact provider source-independence law. Canonical formation/typing agreement proves uniformly that formation invariance supplies the formation half of every typing goal; under that premise, full local typing invariance is equivalent to the isolated target-term HEq objective.

title: Scoped Identity endpoint alignment
boundary: Canonical formation/typing fold agreement proves that each scoped typing result's formation equals the independently dispatched carrier formation, even when readiness witnesses differ. Endpoint terms can therefore be transported into the exact carrier fiber, and the transport preserves them up to heterogeneous equality. The remaining mutual-recursion/readiness coherence equation connecting those transported endpoints to the outer Identity package is now stated exactly, but not yet derived from the existing generated-agreement provider.

title: Scoped Identity package equality and conditional closure
boundary: Independent carrier and endpoint dispatches form a dependent Identity target package. Carrier formation equality and both endpoint HEq invariants combine into equality of these Sigma packages. Under the exact mutual-recursion path-coherence law from group 100, package congruence closes scoped Identity formation target invariance. Deriving that path law from a strengthened generated-agreement provider remains open.

title: Global scoped formation target invariance
boundary: A mutual recursor with the dispatcher-parametric formation motive and a trivial auxiliary typing motive combines the local base, unit, Pi, Sigma, and Identity closures. Consequently global scoped typing target invariance plus the exact Identity recursive path-coherence law imply target invariance for every coherent formation derivation. Proving global typing invariance and deriving the path law remain the two premises.

title: Scoped typing recursive normalization and Lambda boundary
boundary: The public scoped typing dispatcher target term is definitionally equal, up to its dependent type, to the recursively generated anchored output for every typing derivation. This permits constructor arguments to use the recursive normal form directly. For Lambda, the remaining non-definitional step is isolated exactly: agreement must identify the mutual-recursion aligned body term with the independently formation-aligned body target before lambda abstraction.

title: Scoped Lambda target-package invariance and conditional closure
boundary: Canonical anchoring transfers formation invariance in both directions between typing and formation dispatch. Public and recursively generated target-term invariance are equivalent. A dependent Lambda package binds the domain, codomain, and transported body term; package equality follows from domain formation and body typing invariance. Consequently both term-only and full Lambda typing invariance close under the exact recursive term-coherence law isolated in group 103.

title: Scoped Refl target-package invariance and conditional closure
boundary: A dependent Refl package binds a carrier target and its formation-aligned endpoint term. Carrier formation and endpoint typing invariance imply package equality. Identity path coherence aligns the outer formation, after which proof irrelevance derives the Refl recursive term law automatically. Thus the complete scoped Refl typing case requires Identity path coherence only; no independent Refl coherence premise remains.

title: Scoped Apply target package and instantiation boundary
boundary: Target terms transport directly to arbitrary equal semantic formation targets, and reindexing a typing fiber preserves its term up to HEq. The complete dependent Apply package binds domain, codomain, function, argument, result formation, and semantic instantiation equality. The scoped instantiate-agreement provider proves that equality at recursive inputs, formation-cast term preservation transports it through the public dispatcher boundary, and those results now assemble the public external package. Package invariance and final Apply term closure remain.
